question: Why Is My Account Page Blank or Broken?
metaDescription: Usually the My Account shortcode is missing from the assigned page, or a theme/plugin conflict is breaking its endpoint-based navigation.
shortAnswer: The My Account page relies on the [woocommerce_my_account] shortcode being present on whichever page is assigned that role, and its various sections (orders, addresses, account details) work through WordPress "endpoints" appended to that page's URL — if the shortcode is missing, the page will simply be empty, and if endpoint routing is broken (often a permalink issue), sub-sections like order history can fail to load even though the main page appears fine.

image.alt: A My Account page rendering blank because its shortcode is missing or its endpoint-based section routing is broken

bodyHtml:
Why This Happens

The My Account experience isn't a single static page — it's one page containing the [woocommerce_my_account] shortcode, with individual sections (Orders, Downloads, Addresses, Account details) handled through WordPress query-var-based endpoints appended to that page's base URL. Anything that removes the shortcode, breaks the page assignment, or disrupts endpoint routing (commonly a stale permalink structure) can leave the whole experience or specific sections broken.

Common Causes

  • The shortcode accidentally removed from the page during a content edit, or the wrong page assigned as "My Account" under WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced.
  • Stale permalink rewrite rules, the same class of issue behind several other WooCommerce page 404s, breaking the endpoint URLs for specific My Account sections.
  • A theme or page builder wrapping the shortcode in a way that interferes with its own internal navigation and endpoint handling.
  • A plugin conflict (particularly membership, subscription, or custom-account plugins that hook into My Account) breaking a specific section while leaving others functional.
  • Caching serving a stale version of a page that should be dynamic and customer-specific, similar to the checkout caching issue covered elsewhere.

How to Diagnose and Fix It

  1. Confirm the correct page is assigned under WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced, and that it still contains the [woocommerce_my_account] shortcode.
  2. Go to Settings → Permalinks and click Save to refresh rewrite rules, which resolves many endpoint-related issues.
  3. Check for plugin conflicts if a specific section (not the whole page) is broken, using standard plugin-by-plugin isolation.
  4. Confirm My Account is excluded from page caching, since it needs to render fresh, customer-specific content on every load.

Customers unable to access their account or order history? See WooCommerce fixes.
